root_cause.text: The xfrm6_rcv_encap() function fails to release the reference count on a destination entry returned by ip6_route_input_lookup() when the lookup resolves to an error route, causing a resource leak when packets are dropped due to dst->error being set.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that ip6_route_input_lookup() returns a referenced dst entry even for error routes (dst->error set). The original code at line 91 checks `if (dst->error)` and jumps to the drop label without calling dst_release(dst), leaving the reference unreleased. The fix adds `dst_release(dst);` before the `goto drop;` statement to properly decrement the reference count before discarding the packet. This is a classic reference counting bug where an acquired resource (the dst reference) is not released on all error paths.

intent_record.what: Added explicit dst_release(dst) call before the goto drop statement when dst->error is non-zero, wrapping the error check in braces.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the destination routing entry allocated by ip6_route_input_lookup() is properly released back to the kernel's reference counting system when an error is detected, preventing a resource leak. Previously, the error path would jump to drop without decrementing the reference count on the dst object.
